record.title: Graphics backing and scanout have different owners
record.method: Fault-state capture, task page-table walk and independent memory reservations
record.observation: A graphics pool was advertised at an unbacked legacy physical address. Later experiments distinguished user-write permissions, source backing and live scanout; separating default-surface storage removed a source/destination alias.
record.limits: Successful backing and copies do not imply a complete GPU, display driver or stable interactive session.

exhibits.title: Before: a valid translation into an unbacked legacy pool
exhibits.interpretation: The faulting address was translated. Its physical destination belonged to the legacy graphics layout, not to backed native RAM.

exhibits.title: After: separate physical ownership ranges
exhibits.interpretation: These are QEMU diagnostic reservations. Separating source backing from destination scanout prevents an A → B → A presentation from overwriting A while displaying B. The earlier address correction and the later ownership correction solve different defects.

excerpts.note: Selected fields transcribed verbatim. Dotted keys identify their original JSON paths; unselected fields are omitted.

excerpts.content:
| Region | Half-open physical range | Ownership |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Modeled RAM | `0x40000000–0x60000000` | QEMU's 512 MiB RAM |
| XNU advertised memory | `0x50000000–0x57400000` | Includes staged kernel; first-free boundary is `0x506c0000` |
| Native scanout | `0x57e00000–0x57e96000` | Existing 320×480 framebuffer |
| Separate default surface (later correction) | `0x57f00000–0x57f96000` | CPU-rendered CoreSurface backing |
| Relocated graphics pool | `0x58000000–0x58c00000` | Reserved for original CoreSurface allocations |

[…]

The previous adapter used scanout RAM as the default CoreSurface backing.
Copying another surface into scanout therefore overwrote the default source,
and returning to the default surface skipped copying. The source now requires
a distinct, page-aligned default allocation with validated nonoverlapping
32-bit ranges, and copies every selected non-null surface. A host regression
executes setup and A → B → A presentation, checking whole-frame equality and
unchanged default-source contents alongside one-shot console ownership.
